bridge_reviews.comment: Approved. Candidate-v2 removes the unrequested Hessian outcome and content block while retaining supports_item_ids=[RC-002]. The local-minimum definition and gradient construction remain correct, and the worked calculation grad f(x,y)=(2x+y,x)^T with grad f(1,2)=(4,1)^T is correct. The revised MIT OCW locators no longer misidentify Definition 20.1 as Hessian evidence, and the two reachable MIT sources cover the local-minimum and gradient prerequisites. The bridge now prepares only the vocabulary and calculation needed to read RC-002 and continues to exclude the stationarity theorem, Hessian tests, and GD claims.

The revised BC-02 now correctly states L>0 and quantifies the inequality over all x,y; the mathematical content, boundary, dependency role, and pedagogical sequence are approved. Source revision is still required. SRC-03 is falsely titled 'Lipschitz Functions and Vector-Valued Maps': its URL opens Petersen and Pedersen's The Matrix Cookbook, whose inspected text contains no Lipschitz definition or normed-vector-space mapping section, so it cannot support BC-03. For candidate-v3, remove that source and use the directly accessible UC Berkeley Econ 204 Lecture 4 slides at https://eml.berkeley.edu/~cshannon/e204_22/lec4sl-marked.pdf, Definition 5 on printed p.23 (PDF p.44), which explicitly defines Lipschitz functions between normed vector spaces for all input pairs. Bind BC-02 to the Berkeley generic-map definition; bind BC-03 to both Berkeley's generic definition and Cornell's gradient-specific statement; bind BC-04 to Berkeley plus Stanford's norm material. Do not alter the approved teaching text or add descent/convergence content.

Approved. The teaching content, outcomes, exclusions, profile demand, and RC-006 binding remain semantically unchanged from the previously approved bridge. Stanford's Convex Optimization text directly supports the real-vector inner product, convex combinations, and convex-set definition; BC-03 and BC-04 are correct direct applications. The shortened evidence-locator wording does not change its cited sections or source-to-content coverage. The bridge remains prerequisite-sized and does not reproduce the Contract's first-order convexity theorem.

Candidate-v2 correctly removes the unsupported dimensionless sentence, preserves kappa=L/mu, and states the positive-denominator assumption and lower-bound arithmetic correctly. The new Cornell source still does not directly support the complete claim: it separately states L>0 and mu>0 and defines kappa=L/mu, but the inspected page does not establish mu<=L, despite the evidence locator claiming that it does. For candidate-v3, replace or supplement SRC-01 with Purdue University Optimization Methods in Machine Learning notes at https://www.math.purdue.edu/~zhan1966/teaching/598/Opt_notes.pdf. Section 2.4, printed p.30, explicitly derives mu<=L from strong convexity and Lipschitz-gradient inequalities and then identifies L/mu as the condition number. Update the evidence locator and bind that source to BC-01 and BC-02; it may also support the direct arithmetic examples and safeguard. Preserve all current teaching text and exclusions, and do not import the source's convergence-rate or matrix-condition-number discussion.

overall_review.comment: Candidate-v2 remains structurally valid with zero deterministic errors and warnings and retains the correct four-bridge demand union and approved model/pathway bindings. The calculus and convex-set bridges are approved. Release is still blocked by two source-provenance defects that the deterministic validator cannot detect: the supposed Waterloo Lipschitz source is actually The Matrix Cookbook and contains no claimed definition, and the Cornell conditioning source does not establish mu<=L. Generate candidate-v3 changing only those two source records, locators, and source_ids/supports_content_ids bindings exactly as authorized above; preserve all approved teaching content and the two approved bridges, rerun deterministic validation, and generate a fresh pending review.
